cohort: The study included 135 pregnant females in their first trimester, aged 18-35 years, with a BMI between 18.5 and 24.9 kg/m2, without chronic medical disorders, attending Zagazig University antenatal care outpatient clinic.
finding: The nutritional health education program effectively increased pregnant females' knowledge, attitude, and practice towards healthy nutrition, which was associated with obtaining optimal weight gain and improving maternal and fetal outcomes, including lower rates of complications and better neonatal health.
mod_finding: Pregnant females with overweight gain during pregnancy had a statistically significant higher cesarean section rate compared to those with optimal weight gain.
followup_time: Up to delivery and immediate post-partum period
